title: A Double Dose Of Bleak, Futuristic Depression

contact_edits.before: The second play, Sea Change -- "a city park, decades from today" - - is a kind of long-range prequel to the first. The two pieces are in fact linked by a single object, a copy of Reader's Digest. (I'm not telling how.) Things are materially better than they will later become, but the rot has already set in; technology is omnipresent, individuality is eroding and life is cheap. Ironically, the person who feels least at home in a world where people have computers literally in the palm of their hands is a former video-game designer. He's been overtaken. He has billion-dollar election- rigging secrets in his briefcase, but he's no match for two young women: a peddler of uplifting pamphlets who can change identities in an instant and a gun-toting adventuress. There are any number of twists and turns. This spy-spoof is less imaginative satire than its companion piece but brisker entertainment. Richings manages to be taut and bemused at the same time, and the two women are all kinds of tough. I blame both plays, or the worlds of both plays, on global warming, as I am surely meant to do. Warm is the new cool. - Until April 29. Call 416-504- 7529 for ticket information.
